title: Electric Cars
objective: After this level you can explain how electric cars work and how they differ from gas cars.
summary: An electric car's battery-powered motor turns the wheels. Over 77% of plug energy reaches them, and regenerative braking runs the motor as a generator to recharge.

cards.headline: By 1900, about a third of the vehicles on the road were electric.
cards.body: Then cheap gasoline cars such as Ford's Model T, and an electric starter that ended hand-cranking, pushed them aside. Now they're back: in 2025, about 1 in 4 new cars sold worldwide was electric, counting plug-in hybrids (IEA). Inside, they run on ideas from Chapter 1.

cards.headline: Battery, motor, wheels
cards.body: An all-electric car has no internal combustion engine at all. A big rechargeable battery pack stores the energy, and an electric traction motor, Level 7's machine for turning electricity into motion, drives the wheels. Nothing burns, so there's no tailpipe and no exhaust. Level 24's four strokes, spark plugs and pistons simply aren't there.

cards.fact: Counting from the plug, an electric car gets over 77% of its energy to the wheels.
cards.context: A gas car gets only about 12%-30% of its fuel's energy to the wheels, as Level 24 showed. The difference is mostly heat: an engine burning fuel loses most of its energy that way, and an electric motor loses far less. Level 2's rule does the accounting: less energy lost means more of it moving you.

cards.headline: Braking that charges the battery
cards.body: Here's the clever part. When an electric car slows down, the turning wheels spin its motor, and the motor runs as a generator, just as Level 8 said a motor run backwards would. It makes electricity that goes back into the battery, and doing that work helps slow the car. This is regenerative braking: energy that braking would normally waste gets saved.

mascot.line: This is Level 8's idea again: run a motor backwards and it's a generator.

questions.prompt: What turns the wheels of an all-electric car?

options.label: A small gas engine inside it
options.rationale: An all-electric car burns no fuel.

options.label: A motor powered by a battery pack
A steam turbine under the hood
options.rationale: No steam here: a motor does the work.

options.label: Solar panels on the roof
options.rationale: The energy comes from a battery pack.

questions.explanation: An electric traction motor, powered by a rechargeable battery pack, drives the wheels.

questions.prompt: Counting from the plug, why does an electric car get more of its energy to the wheels than a gas car gets from its fuel?

options.label: Its battery makes extra energy
options.rationale: Batteries store energy; they cannot create it.

options.label: Its motor loses far less energy as heat

questions.explanation: Over 77% versus about 12%-30%: an engine burning fuel loses most of its energy as heat, while a motor loses much less.

questions.prompt: Regenerative braking depends on an idea from Level 8. Which one?

options.label: Current makes a magnetic field
options.rationale: That was Level 7, and it runs the motor.

options.label: AC beat DC in the War of the Currents
A motor run backwards works as a generator
Batteries die when their chemicals run out

questions.explanation: Spun by the wheels, the motor becomes a generator, turning motion into electricity for the battery.
